review_scope: All seven supplied TeX inputs were read completely, including their proofs. All six reconstructed inputs receive two complete revised mathematical/editorial reads, including every proof; the second follows the first compilation and visual review. Bounded changed interfaces in Chapters 1, 13, 27, 32 and 33 were reread. This is a supplied-result integration, not a new complete rewrite of those chapters. The six inputs add seventeen statement/example environments, twelve proofs and fifty-four labels. All pre-existing labeled statements and proofs in the eight changed existing inputs are preserved byte-for-byte; the obstacle-envelope input changes spacing only. The bibliography is unchanged.
mathematical_boundaries: The new proofs distinguish prescribed nonminimal logarithmic type from poles intrinsic to a minimal type, equation scalar uniqueness from potential uniqueness, Hölder finite-distance control from continuity alone, and a necessary exceptional density vanishing order from sufficiency for smoothness. The logarithmic and iterated-logarithmic equality endpoints are checked from exact density integrals. The range n < d <= 2n gives a bounded continuous minimal residual with a complete regular end. The exceptional density threshold uses data bounded above and below by positive constants; finite-p sharpness is an upper limitation, without an endpoint assertion. Resolved logarithmic coefficients may be real; they are not silently identified with the book's rational-coefficient analytic singularities.
dependencies: Complete internal input reads cover the Hölder regularization proof, ample-locus smoothness, psh exponential integrability, and the Chapter 2 mass-invariance theorem and proof. Bounded dependency reads cover the resolved bounded-residual lemma, holomorphic-disk/modification descent and L1 pullback arguments, the Chapter 10 bounded existence input, the Chapter 13 local-density boundary, and the Chapter 27 incomplete-metric and normal-length arguments. The changed Chapter 32 regularity subsection and completeness/flow paragraphs were reread, along with the corresponding Chapter 33 uniqueness and regularity notes. These dependency scopes are not whole-chapter audits. Existing bounded-product, extended-product and removable-singularity statements are reused; their duplicate source formulations are not inserted again. Existing closed full-mass uniqueness and minimal-mass dependencies remain identified in the final history chapter, with a short new internal-use clarification and no new source-paper citation.
